summary: John Penry Lewis was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his B.A. from Queen's University Belfast (~1872–1876) and served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1877 to 1910.

John Peter Jones worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Case Western Reserve University (~1871–1875) and Andover Theological Seminary (M.A., ~1875), later serving as Principal of Pasumalai Seminary (1892–1914) and Professor of Indian Missions at Hartford Seminary (1914).
John Peter Wade was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh. In 1784, he served as an Assistant Medical Surgeon for the East India Company.

John Peterson is an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts at Kiel University (~1995–1997), the University of Zurich (~1997–1999), the University of Osnabrück (~2001–2009), and the University of Leipzig (~2009–2011).

Indologist John Pickford studied at Brasenose College and the University of Oxford (M.A., 1865) under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai (until 1872), and as a professor at the University of Madras.

John Playfair was an Indologist and mathematician who studied at the University of St Andrews, St Mary's College, and the University of Edinburgh. He co-founded the Royal Society of Edinburgh (1783) and served as Professor of Mathematics at Edinburgh (1785–1818).

John Powers specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Holy Cross, McMaster, and Virginia (under Jeffrey Hopkins), he held posts at Australian National University (1995–2016), Deakin University (2016–2022), and the University of Melbourne (2022).

John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Columbia University, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb alongside traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama.

John R. McRae specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Cornell University (~1988–1995), Indiana University Bloomington (~1995–2004), Soka University (2004), and Komazawa University.
John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
John Robert Gardner works in Indology and computational fields. He held posts at the University of Iowa (attested 1996) and at Emory University as an XML Engineer (attested 1999–2000).

John Ronald Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2004).

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard University under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, and held a long-term post at Colgate University (~1972–2012), including teaching at Chapel House.

John S. Strong works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Frank E. Reynolds. He served as Dana Professor Emeritus at Bates College (1987–1988).

John Sampson was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as the Librarian at the University of Liverpool from 1892 to 1928 and was awarded degrees from Liverpool (Hon. M.A. ~1907, D.Litt. ~1930) and Oxford (D.Litt. ~1909).

John Scudder Chandler worked in Indology and linguistics, earning a B.A. from Yale (~1866–1870). He served as acting principal of Pasumalai Seminary (1890–1892), Fellow at the University of Madras (1913–1922), and director of the Language School at Kodaikanal (1924–1928).

John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Wellington College, RMA Sandhurst, and under John Richardson. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at RMC Sandhurst (1805–1809) and Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore was an Indology and history/archaeology figure who succeeded William Jones to serve as President of The Asiatic Society in 1794.

John Shortt was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Madras Medical College (~1843–1846) and Aberdeen (M.D., 1850). He served as Assistant Apothecary for the East India Company (~1846) and Assistant Surgeon at Madras University (1854–1878).

John Sinclair Stevenson was a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Clifton College, Lincoln College, Edinburgh, and Princeton Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary for the Presbyterian Church in Ireland from 1894 to 1924.
